idea: China energy policy interpretation briefing for Western investors
buyer: Energy and macro PMs, policy teams at funds
pain: Chinese policy documents are published in Chinese and misread in translation
channel: Fund network plus father's policy contacts
verdict: Direct use of her father's rarest asset, with genuine scarcity value and subscription economics.

why.distribution: Warm fund contacts; the policy access itself does not add distribution, only credibility.
why.demand: Funds buy China macro and policy research today from several providers.
why.fmf: Language plus policy access plus investment framing; she is not herself a policy specialist.
why.defensibility: Interpretation informed by people inside the policy process is hard to replicate.
why.time_to_revenue: 3-6 months to establish a publication rhythm and credibility.
why.tailwind: China energy policy drives global transition markets, though China exposure is politically fraught for some allocators.
why.ceiling: £1,000/mo x 17 funds = £204k, requiring seventeen institutional subscribers.

ceiling_arithmetic: £1,000/mo x 17 funds = £204k. Seventeen subscribers is more than her warm network typically converts; realistic is 6-8 = £72-96k.
carries: Uses the scarcest thing in her whole network - genuine proximity to Chinese energy policy - in a subscription format.
kills: Subscriber count. £1,000/month needs seventeen funds, beyond typical conversion from a 50-person network.
test: Send two energy PMs an interpreted briefing on a recent policy document.
test_pass: One says it corrected their understanding and asks about pricing.
test_fail: They say their China analyst covers it.
